rows.grounds: past participle indicating emergence or departure
indeclinable indicating outward location or direction
compound describing exceptional adeptness in expressive signs
particle introducing a simile or wondering comparison

items.question: To what expressive manifestation is Gaṅgā likened as she emerges outward in pure form?
premises: Gaṅgā is described as having gone forth outside.
Gaṅgā is characterized as extremely skilled in gestures.
Gaṅgā is portrayed as having pure limbs.
items.inference: Gaṅgā is presented through a simile as an outwardly manifest, pure, and expressively eloquent presence.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the implied comparison introduced by kimu is not explicitly stated in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Gaṅgā, pure-limbed and highly skilled in gestures, has come forth outside, as if manifesting in an expressive form.
